unit_dependency_entry.context_note: The proposed bounds are described as expected approximations, not proved global inequalities.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: Equations (L.1)-(L.7) are layout-sensitive; the asymptotic status and sign-alternation mechanism are stated clearly.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Special-function series evaluate Dedekind xi derivative inputs
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Theta-integral pieces are rewritten using incomplete gamma, error, and exponential-integral functions, and special derivative values are identified as inputs to Dedekind Li logarithmic derivatives.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Asymptotic corrections can tighten S1's linear term and suggest alternating approximations, but further refinement of S1 leaves S2 magnitude control as the decisive missing ingredient.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The Euler-Maclaurin correction series is explicitly divergent and the proposed upper/lower approximations are not stated as proved uniform bounds.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Euler-Maclaurin refines the solved term without removing the central obstruction

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Euler-Maclaurin separates S1 into a computable digamma integral and Bernoulli derivative corrections. The correction signs suggest alternating upper and lower approximations, but the same representation displays its own obstruction: the series is asymptotic and generally divergent.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source defines the summand f(k), derives its arbitrary derivatives, and applies Euler-Maclaurin with vanishing derivatives at infinity. Using a previously evaluated integral gives S1(n) as n[ψ(n)+γ]/2 plus Bernoulli corrections; the first truncations (L.7a)-(L.7b) are proposed as approximate upper and lower bounds, with alternating signs for large n.
directed.conceptual_reading: The representation decomposes a discrete sum into a smooth bulk term and local endpoint corrections. It refines asymptotics systematically, while divergence means the useful object is a controlled truncation rather than the formal infinite series.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is discrete S1 sum → Euler-Maclaurin integral plus endpoint derivatives → digamma main term plus Bernoulli corrections; explicit derivatives of f make successive refinements available.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The source calls the candidate bounds expected approximations, not proved uniform inequalities, and emphasizes that the correction series generally diverges. No remainder estimate or optimal-truncation analysis is supplied, and refining S1 does not bound the separate S2 obstruction.
directed.uncertainty: The asymptotic status and sign-alternation mechanism are clear, but exact formulas (L.1)-(L.7) are layout-sensitive and their use as rigorous bounds would require an independent remainder argument.

supported: The source defines f(k), derives arbitrary derivatives, and inserts them into Euler-Maclaurin to express S1 as a digamma bulk term plus Bernoulli endpoint corrections.
It explicitly says the sums are asymptotic and generally divergent, and labels (L.7a)-(L.7b) only expected approximate upper and lower bounds.
The eventual sign alternation is tied to the Bernoulli signs after the source's sufficiently-large-n simplification.
inference: The smooth-bulk versus endpoint-correction decomposition is a faithful conceptual reading of Euler-Maclaurin.
Finite truncation is the practically relevant object, but the source supplies no theorem controlling its remainder.
unsupported_or_imported: Calling the useful object a 'controlled truncation' overstates the evidence because the candidate itself notes that no remainder estimate or optimal-truncation analysis is supplied.
The statement that refining S1 does not bound a separate S2 obstruction is imported from outside this exact Appendix L span.
context_or_ocr_risk: Exact derivative and correction formulas in (L.1)-(L.7) are layout-sensitive, although the asymptotic status is explicit in prose.
missed_mechanism: The distinction between sign alternation of formal correction terms for sufficiently large n and a rigorous alternating-series remainder bound must remain explicit.
revision_instructions: Replace 'controlled truncation' with 'finite or heuristically chosen truncation requiring independent remainder control.'
Remove the imported S2 claim from the unit analysis or label it as external synthesis context.
Do not promote the expected approximate bounds to proved uniform inequalities.
